en: Never look directly at the Sun without certified eclipse glasses, as its intense light can permanently damage your retinas.
Boil floodwater before drinking it to kill harmful bacteria washed into the water cycle during heavy typhoons.
If you hear thunder during a storm, immediately seek shelter inside a fully enclosed building to avoid lightning strikes.
Drink plenty of water and stay in the shade when the heat index exceeds 40°C to prevent heatstroke.
Drop, cover, and hold on under a sturdy table during an earthquake to protect your head from falling objects.
During a typhoon signal, stay indoors away from windows to protect yourself from flying debris and strong winds.
Wear gloves when handling compost or potting soil to avoid inhaling fungal spores that can cause respiratory infections.
Avoid playing in abandoned mining areas, as exposed rocks can leach toxic heavy metals like mercury into the soil.
Always wear closed-toe shoes when hiking on volcanic rocks to prevent cuts from sharp, glassy obsidian.
Stay away from the shoreline during a spring tide, as the aligned Sun and Moon create unusually high, dangerous waves.
Turn off bright outdoor lights at night to reduce light pollution, helping you sleep better and see stars clearly.
Cover your water storage containers tightly to prevent mosquitoes from breeding in stagnant rainwater, which is part of the water cycle.
